sources.entry: LingShu - Open-source, model-agnostic macOS agent for verified code, documents, slides, and computer actions. [![Open-Source Software][OSS Icon]](https://github.com/RoyZhao1991/LingShu) ![Freeware][Freeware Icon]

summary.name: LingShu
summary.one_liner: LingShu is an open-source, model-agnostic macOS execution agent that lets you bring your own LLM (OpenAI, Claude, DeepSeek, MiniMax or compatible endpoints) to produce verified code, office documents, slides and authorized Mac workflows.
keywords: ai agent that controls mac apps
use_cases: Generate a one-page DOCX project brief and verify it
Create editable PPTX slide decks from a brief
Produce verified software with a local agent
Use your own OpenAI, Claude or DeepSeek API token with a macOS agent
summary.what_it_does: The page describes a native macOS app and agent runtime that takes a brief through understanding, planning, execution, collaboration and verification. Work is dispatched to workers, tools, local files and authorized Mac apps, and pauses for login, QR scans, file choices or confirmations. Deliverables such as PPTX, DOCX, PDF, media and code are registered as artifacts and sent to an independent checker, with a built-in local preview. The model layer is replaceable: OpenAI, Anthropic, DeepSeek, MiniMax and compatible endpoints share the same agent layer, and the user supplies their own API token.
notable: Full native app and agent runtime open source under Apache-2.0, written in Swift, with over 1,500 tests
Model-agnostic: works with OpenAI, Claude, DeepSeek, MiniMax or compatible endpoints via your own token
Goes beyond code: editable PPTX and DOCX output, built-in preview, and an artifact ledger with independent checker
Installable via Homebrew cask; Apple notarized
caveats: Bring-your-own-key: inference credits are not included, so model API costs are separate
Alpha/public beta stage; the page advises reviewing permissions, keeping backups and checking important deliverables before external use
Official repository is listed as all rights reserved for the code outside the open-sourced runtime, per the page's comparison table
